post.title: A tax extension gives you zero extra days to pay
post.ig:
A tax extension gives you zero extra days to pay.

For 2026 taxes, returns and payments are due April 15, 2027; Form 4868 moves only the filing deadline, to October 15, 2027.
Unpaid tax collects IRS interest from April 15 (7% a year as of late 2026) plus a late-payment penalty of 0.5% a month.
The late-filing penalty is 5% a month, about 10 times bigger. Example: owe $4,000, file and pay 5 months late: $1,000 in penalties with no extension vs $100 with one (interest not included).

Sources: IRS failure-to-file and failure-to-pay penalty pages; IRS IR-2026-98 (Q4 2026 interest); IRS extension guidance.

Form 4868 moves the filing deadline for 2026 returns from April 15 to October 15, 2027, but the tax is still due April 15, with IRS interest (7% as of late 2026) and a 0.5% monthly late-payment penalty on any unpaid balance. The late-filing penalty is 5% a month, so in an example of owing $4,000 and paying 5 months late, penalties are $1,000 with no extension versus $100 with one (sources: IRS penalty pages, IR-2026-98).
